prompt: On disposable Ubuntu, use read-only commands to analyze one non-sensitive existing path as your normal user, then design but do not apply a least-privilege repair for a hypothetical service identity that lacks required access.
deliverables: A sanitized environment card naming Ubuntu/kernel, caller identity, namespace boundary, chosen path, intended operation, authorization, and time.
A component-by-component path diagram showing resolution, numeric owner/group, applicable mode class, required directory operation, final-object operation, ACL mask, mount, and LSM gates.
A command evidence table for id, proc status capabilities, readlink, namei, stat, findmnt, and getfacl when available, including proves and does not prove.
A hypothetical service credential and a manually reasoned allow/deny result without changing users or permissions.
A narrow proposed fix with owner, rollback, positive test, negative unauthorized test, monitoring, and prevention.
A no-mutation cleanup statement, redactions, limitations, and assistance disclosure.
evidenceRequirements: Use numeric UID/GID evidence as well as names and distinguish the current shell from the hypothetical service.
Explain read, write, and execute separately for regular files and directories.
Apply only one owner/group/other class at each inode and include supplementary groups.
Explain ACL mask, read-only/noexec/nosuid mount options, capabilities, and AppArmor/SELinux as separate layers even if absent.
Do not run sudo, chmod, chown, setfacl, setcap, remount, policy-disable, or production-path commands.
Do not inspect this assessment implementation or a model answer while producing the independent work.

rubric.observableEvidence: Uses authorized non-sensitive read-only scope with exact identity/time and no mutation.
Correctly evaluates every directory component and final operation.
Separates modes, ACL mask, mount, capabilities, namespaces, and LSM policy.
Proposes a narrow owned fix with rollback and positive/negative tests.
Transfers numeric identity reasoning to systemd, container, Kubernetes, and storage boundaries.
